answer: I would run a harbor admission list built on a voyage log. A new agent starts read-only and must finish 30 small jobs that independent checkers verify on chain over 21 days, each logged with input, output, and checker signature. Only then does it earn an opal pass for full trading, and the pass decays after 60 idle days. A farmer wanting 1,000 fake agents would need 30,000 verified jobs, about $60,000 in fees at $2 per job plus three weeks of waiting, for identities that still expire. It is like a port that only waves through captains who have actually sailed in before.
